input: Replace the smoke-stained ceiling tiles in the kitchen

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether it is a full ceiling replacement or just a few stained tiles changes the scale of the job entirely — materials needed, time, and effort differ dramatically.
The ceiling tile system type (drop/suspended grid vs. glue-up vs. tongue-and-groove) determines the removal method, replacement process, and what tiles to buy.
Whether this is a DIY project or involves hiring a contractor affects planning, budget, scheduling, and the level of detail needed in the task plan.
A defined budget sets boundaries on tile material choices, whether to hire help, and how many tiles can realistically be replaced.
Knowing if matching replacement tiles have already been sourced — or need to be found — determines whether procurement is a key first step.
The user may want an exact match to existing tiles, a cosmetic upgrade, or a completely different style, which changes what products to target.
Understanding the end goal — purely functional fix, rental-ready, or home-sale presentation — sets the quality bar and influences every decision in the plan.

gold.taskDescription: Remove and replace the smoke-stained ceiling tiles in the kitchen with clean, matching, or upgraded tiles.

questions.title: How many tiles need replacing — a few or the whole ceiling?
questions.description: Determine the scope: spot replacement of visibly stained tiles only, or a full ceiling overhaul.

questions.title: What type of ceiling tile system is currently installed?
questions.description: Identify whether the kitchen has a suspended/drop grid, glue-up, nail-up, or another tile system, as this dictates the removal and installation method.

questions.title: Will you do this yourself or hire a contractor?
questions.description: Establish whether this is a DIY task or a managed professional job, which shapes the entire plan structure.

questions.title: What is your budget for materials and labour?
questions.description: Set the financial ceiling (no pun intended) to guide tile selection and decisions around professional help.

questions.title: Do you already have replacement tiles, or do they still need to be sourced?
questions.description: Determine whether procurement is a pending step or if materials are already on hand and ready to install.

questions.title: Should the new tiles match existing ones or is a style change welcome?
questions.description: Clarify whether the goal is a seamless like-for-like repair or an opportunity to update the kitchen's ceiling aesthetic.

questions.title: What is the finished ceiling ultimately needed for — daily use, rental, or sale?
questions.description: Understand the end-use context to set the appropriate quality and finish standard for the completed job.
